newsitem.title: UK: ISDA calls on Italy to legislate on netting.
newsitem.headline: ISDA calls on Italy to legislate on netting.

text.p: The International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) said on Wednesday it was urging Italian authorities to take legislative action to ensure close-out netting was enforceable in Italy.

"Although there is legal opinion in Italy that close-out netting under a master agreement would be enforceable under Italian law in the event of the insolvency of an Italian counterparty, a number of Italian lawyers appear to take a different view," the industry group said in a statement.
"Market participants in other EU member states, and indeed in other leading jurisdictions around the world, are aware of this debate," ISDA said.
It said that as a result there was substantial uncertainty among international market players on the enforceability of close-out netting in Italy.

Netting is the amalgamation of obligations between two or more parties -- a broker and a customer, for example -- into a net amount. Close-out netting refers to using netting techniques to conclude transactions when one counterparty defaults.
ISDA said the current situation has put Italian financial institutions, government bodies and businesses at a competitive disadvantage.

This is because EU central banks and those of other major centres have been unwilling to permit supervised credit institutions in their jurisdictions to net against Italian counterparties for capital purposes, it said.

"Due to recently adopted or pending legislation in a number of member states of the EU, Italy will shortly be out of step on the netting question with the other leading economies of Europe and potential EMU participants," ISDA said.
